newsitem.title: PERU: One Swedish, two Peru firms bid in Mahr Tunel sale.
newsitem.headline: One Swedish, two Peru firms bid in Mahr Tunel sale.

text.p: Sweden's Boliden and local miners Morococha and Volcan were the only three firms to make formal bids Monday to buy Peru's Mahr Tunel mining unit, privatization officials said.
The winner of the sale, by Peruvian state miner Centromin, will be announced Friday.
Peruvian state miner Centromin has set a $50 million minimum bid price, and a minimum investment commitment of $60 million over five years, for the privatization of its Mahr Tunel SA subsidiary.

A handful of other companies -- including Mexico's Industrias Penoles SA and Grupo Mexico SA, Switzerland's Glencore International, Australia's Savage Resources Ltd, the United States' Sunshine Mining and Refining Co, and Peru's Minsur SA and Arcata Hoschild - had also originally expressed interest in bidding.

Mahr Tunel SA controls the San Cristobal and Andaychagua mines, which lie close to each other in the central Peruvian highlands. Last year, San Cristobal produced 680,000 dry tonnes of ore containing zinc, lead, copper and silver, while Andaychagua produced about 395,000 dry tonnes of ore with silver, lead and zinc.
